title: Introduce transactional release pipelines + modular pipeline templates
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduce atomic release orchestration and modular pipeline templates; improves rollback safety and reduces release flakiness. Non-breaking to consumer APIs; infra change only.
description: Context: Our current release flow relies on a long, linear GitHub Actions pipeline that stages and publishes artifacts in multiple disconnected steps. This causes partial rollouts, inconsistent artifact sets, and makes rollbacks manual. Motivation: reduce release blast radius, make rollbacks automated, and make pipeline pieces reusable for Dedicated/Private release variants. Changes in this PR: 1) Add a transactional release orchestration step (actions/release-orchestrator) that stages artifacts in a single transaction and only publishes on successful verification. 2) Split monolithic .github/workflows/release.yml into modular templates under .github/workflow-templates/ (build.yml, verify.yml, promote.yml, rollback.yml). 3) Introduce a lightweight release manifest (ci/release-manifests/v1.jsonnet) that enumerates artifact sets and verification hooks. 4) Add a new library action at .github/actions/prepare-artifact that produces hermetic release bundles (sha256 checksummed). 5) Backfill tests and integration matrix to validate transactional semantics across runners. Migration notes and rollout plan: - This is a backend change that affects CI only; consumers should see no API change. - Staged rollout: opt-in on a per-repo basis using repository_dispatch -> when stable, flip main release.yml to use the templates. - Oncall runbook updated: docs/oncall/ci-transactional-releases.md. - Rollback: the promotable artifacts are moved to a temporary namespace and sweep/rollback is implemented via the promote/rollback templates. Testing: - Unit tests for the action are under .github/actions/prepare-artifact/test (mocked runner). - Integration testing performed in benchmark-lab and perf-canary repos; results included below. Checklist: - [x] Modularize workflows and extract templates - [x] Implement release-orchestrator action - [x] Add manifest schema and validator - [x] Add unit and integration tests - [x] Update oncall docs and runbooks Compatibility and risk: Low risk to runtime code; medium risk to release engineers during rollout. The new action is idempotent; we added guards to prevent double-promotion. Related work: ENG-8213 (release orchestration), ENG-8299 (ci hygiene), SUP-1427 (incident root cause reduction).

review_conversation: Ethan Rogers (2026-02-19): Can you clarify how the orchestrator prevents double-promotion if a job is retried?

Maya Patel (2026-02-19): The orchestrator writes a lock key to the artifacts namespace with the release id; retries check that key and only proceed if the originating run id matches. Added unit test for retry behavior.
